stemMd: A town reports that complaints about rubbish collection fell after it replaced a phone line with an online form. It claims the service improved. Which question is most important?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Was the announcement printed on white paper?

options.label: B
options.textMd: How many letters are in the town’s name?

options.label: C
options.textMd: Did the rubbish trucks have numbered plates?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Did the form use a blue or green border?

options.label: E
options.textMd: Did the new reporting method make it harder for residents to submit complaints?

explanationMd: Complaint counts reflect both problems and the ability or willingness to report them. Replacing a phone line may reduce access for some residents, lowering complaints even if service quality is unchanged. The reporting mechanism must be examined before attributing the decline to improvement.

distractorRationale.d: Colour alone is not the key access issue.
distractorRationale.b: This is irrelevant to complaint reporting.
distractorRationale.c: Vehicle identification does not explain the reporting change.
distractorRationale.a: Paper colour does not evaluate service quality or reporting barriers.
